controls.name: Portal TLS Service Profile Bound
controls.description:
A GlobalProtect portal with no SSL/TLS service profile bound to it. Nobody has decided what the portal will negotiate, so remote users get whatever floor the platform falls back to, and a reviewer reading the portal's own record is shown a posture the handshake does not deliver.

THE CLAUSE IS ON THE BINDING AND ON NOTHING ELSE, which is narrower than this control's catalogue text and deliberately so. The text asserts four things in one sentence - a binding, a TLS 1.2+ floor, a CA-issued certificate and a monitored expiry - and three of them belong to controls whose object IS the value in question: PAN-CRT-005 owns the floor on the service profile itself and names GlobalProtect among the services it floors, PAN-CRT-009 owns the algorithm selections on the same profile, and PAN-CRT-001 owns the expiry. What the portal's own leaf holds is a NAME and nothing more, so the binding is the whole of what this row can assert.

THE BINDING IS MANDATORY ON A COMMITTED PORTAL, measured three ways, so a row this fires on is one whose configuration a collection did not carry rather than a portal an operator left unbound. That is a real row in a real estate and it is what the derived column exists to report; the finding says so, and `mandatory_keys_present` beside the row is what records it. The clause is written on the derived verdict and NOT on `ssl_tls_service_profile is_empty` on purpose - whether the absence operator matches a column that was never populated is a property of the query layer and not of the device.

ON A SHARED INTERFACE THE PORTAL'S OWN SETTING IS NOT WHAT IS IN FORCE. The vendor states twice that where a gateway and a portal terminate on the same interface and do not share a certificate profile and an SSL/TLS service profile, the gateway's configuration takes precedence during the SSL handshake. So the interface-sharing question decides whose transport settings apply, and it is the engineer's to answer.

THE SECOND HALF OF THIS CONTROL IS NOT EXPRESSED AND IS NOT DROPPED SILENTLY. That the certificate the portal presents chains to an authority the connecting endpoint already trusts, before anything has been deployed to that endpoint, has NO COLUMN: the firewall holds the certificate's own fields and not the trust stores of the endpoints that will reach it, and the address users actually reach the portal at is not a firewall fact either. It is answered by the engineer, so a clean result on this control is not evidence of a trusted chain.

AN APPLICABILITY QUESTION DELIBERATELY NOT MADE A CLAUSE: which of these portals face a network the customer does not control. A portal on an internal segment carries the same configuration and not the same risk, and no column distinguishes them - a clause on an unanswered question would SUPPRESS the control rather than qualify it.
controls.rationale: The first thing a new endpoint does is reach the portal over HTTPS with no GlobalProtect configuration on it yet, so the portal's transport settings are the only thing standing between a remote user and an interception on the one connection where nothing else is in place to notice it.
controls.audit: Network > GlobalProtect > Portals. Open the portal the finding names and read `portal-config/ssl-tls-service-profile`. A blank value on a committed portal is not a device state - the firewall refuses to commit a portal without it - so check whether the configuration read for this appliance carried the portal's `portal-config` subtree at all before reporting it as unbound. Then open the profile the name points at and check its floor against PAN-CRT-005, which owns that assertion. Where a gateway terminates on the same interface, read the gateway's profile too: the vendor says the gateway's wins.
controls.remediation: Bind an SSL/TLS service profile to the portal. Where a gateway terminates on the same interface, bind the SAME certificate profile and SSL/TLS service profile to both, which is the vendor's own recommendation and the only way the portal's record and the handshake agree. Obtaining a trusted certificate is a separate piece of work from binding a profile - a reissuance rather than a configuration write - which is why this control does not carry it.

queries.name: Baseline
queries.short_description: A GlobalProtect portal with no SSL/TLS service profile name bound to it.

controls.name: Portal Authentication Demands More Than A Password
controls.description:
A row of a GlobalProtect portal's client-authentication table that will admit an endpoint class on a password alone, or on whichever of a password and a client certificate the endpoint can produce. A portal that one stolen password opens hands the attacker the agent configuration and the network behind it, and the reconnection credential the portal then issues turns that single phished password into access that outlives the session it was stolen in.

THE SUBJECT IS THE ROW AND NOT THE PORTAL, and that is this control's central decision. The table is KEYED BY THE ENDPOINT CLASS - `Any`, `Browser`, `Satellite`, or one of eleven per-platform names the leaf also references - so one portal can demand both factors of one class and neither of another. Measured: two rows of ONE portal in this lab sit at `high` and at no finding at all. A control at the portal grain would report one verdict for both, could not say which class was weak, and would show the compliant row beside the failing one as though they agreed.

GRADED ON ONE DERIVED COLUMN AND NOT ON TWO CLAUSES, because the failing condition is a DISJUNCTION - no certificate profile bound to the portal, OR one bound with a permissive and/or switch - and a clause list is one conjunction with no OR, so two clauses would fire only where both held. `password_only` is the estate's measured state and sits at the baseline; `password_or_certificate` is one tier lower, because the attacker needs only whichever of the two they can obtain; `unknown` fires AT the baseline rather than grading down, because its two candidate readings are the two ENDS of this grading and there is no defensible middle.

THE VENDOR'S POLARITY READS BACKWARDS AND IS KEPT. `yes` on `user-credential-or-client-cert-required` means a password OR a client certificate will do, which is the PERMISSIVE state, and `no` means both are required, which is the hardened one - the device's own help string spells it `No (User Credentials AND Client Certificate Required)`. A reviewer who selected `yes` believing they had the hardened rows selected exactly the permissive ones.

ONE SEVERITY SEPARATES TWO ROWS WHOSE OWN SWITCH VALUES ARE IDENTICAL, and the difference is a leaf on the PARENT portal: whether `portal-config/certificate-profile` binds anything at all. Where it binds nothing there is no second factor for the OR to reach, so a permissive switch means a password is the whole test. That fact is carried down onto each row through the row's own foreign key to its portal, which is a to-one upward walk.

TWO OF THIS CONTROL'S FOUR RANKS ARE NOT PLACEABLE AND BOTH ABSENCES ARE DELIBERATE. Its acceptable minimum - a password verified by an identity service the customer confirms enforces a second factor - IS NOT A VALUE OF ANY COLUMN, because the firewall records WHICH service it asks and never what that service demands. So a row naming a SAML or RADIUS object is not evidence of MFA, and no query here can award it.

THE FALLBACK PATH IS UNEXPRESSED RATHER THAN SATISFIED. The first factor may be an authentication PROFILE or an authentication SEQUENCE - two different objects, both stored by this project - and this column cannot say which. A sequence is tried member by member until one succeeds, so a portal bound to one whose last member is the firewall's own local user database accepts a locally held password whenever the identity service is unreachable. The finding names the bound object so an engineer can resolve it by hand.

AND THE WEAKEST ADMISSION STATE THE DEVICE PERMITS PRODUCES NO FINDING AT ALL. A portal with an EMPTY authentication table demands nothing of anybody, which is weaker than every rank graded here, and it produces no row of this subject to report on. `GlobalProtectPortal.client_auth_row_count` is the only column anywhere that can see it, and a control's queries all compile against one model.
controls.rationale: Portal authentication gates delivery of the agent configuration and of the network behind it, so a password-only path is one phishing email from a working remote-access session, and the credential the portal issues on success keeps that access alive after the password is changed.
controls.audit: Network > GlobalProtect > Portals > the portal the finding names > Authentication. Open the row the finding names - the finding prints the row name, the portal and the endpoint class, because the row name alone is operator-chosen and not unique within a vsys - and read two things together: the and/or switch on the row, remembering that `Yes` is the permissive setting, and `portal-config/certificate-profile` on the portal above it. Then open the authentication object the row names and establish whether it is a profile or a SEQUENCE, and whether the service behind it actually enforces a second factor; neither is a firewall fact.
controls.remediation: Set the row's and/or switch to require both factors - the setting whose label reads `No (User Credentials AND Client Certificate Required)` - and bind a certificate profile to the portal so that a client certificate can be demanded at all. Both are needed: the switch alone demands a certificate the portal cannot check, and the profile alone leaves the row admitting either factor. Repeat for EVERY row of the table, including any fallback row, and check whether the authentication object is a sequence whose last member is the firewall's local user database.

queries.name: Baseline
queries.short_description: A portal authentication row that does not demand both a password and a client certificate of the endpoint class it serves.

queries.name: Admission on a password alone
queries.short_description: The and/or switch is permissive and the portal binds no certificate profile, so a password is the whole of the admission test for this endpoint class.

queries.name: Admission on either factor rather than both
queries.short_description: A certificate profile is bound and the and/or switch is permissive, so the endpoint is admitted on whichever of the two factors it can produce.

queries.name: What this row demands could not be resolved
queries.short_description: The and/or switch is absent from this row, so one of the two inputs the verdict needs is missing and the row's demand was not established.

controls.name: Portal Drives Agents To A Current Version
controls.description:
A GlobalProtect portal whose agent configuration does not tell the endpoint to move to a current app version. An endpoint running a superseded GlobalProtect app carries client vulnerabilities that are already patched and publicly described, and the portal is the only thing that reaches those endpoints - so an estate that does not drive upgrades from there has no mechanism that will ever retire them.

THE SETTING THAT COUNTS IS THE ONE ON THE FIRST AGENT CONFIGURATION AN ENDPOINT MATCHES, because the portal delivers the first match and stops. The collection is a flat entry list with no priority key, so the order is the DOCUMENT order and a consumer that sorts destroys the semantics; the finding names which configuration to edit.

THREE SENTINELS, AND THEY ARE THE REASON THIS CONTROL IS NOT A SINGLE EQUALITY. A naive reading - an equality on a `gp-app-config` entry named after the setting - PASSES EVERY PORTAL THAT HANDS OUT NO AGENT CONFIGURATION AT ALL, which is the measured state of the one portal in this lab that nobody here configured: a missing key matches no equality and the row is dropped silently. `no_agent_configuration` reports it at the baseline. `not_set` reports a configuration that exists and says nothing about upgrades - three sources agree the FORM's default is `Allow with Prompt` and not one of them is a measurement of what the agent does when the member is absent, and the agent is the thing that acts on it. `several_members` reports the wire hazard: the stored list APPENDS rather than replaces on a setting the vendor's own schema marks single-valued, with neither the member value nor the entry name validated at the write, so there is no effective instruction to report.

A FIFTH VENDOR VALUE HAS NO RANK AND IS REPORTED AT THE BASELINE ANYWAY. The device's predefined dictionary and the vendor Help agree on prompt / disabled / manual / transparent / INTERNAL, and the fifth upgrades automatically but waits until the endpoint is connected internally to the corporate network. Whether that converges depends on how often the population is on the corporate network, which is the customer's fact and not the firewall's - so it was left unranked. It still reports, because the assertion is written as the negation of the two ACCEPTABLE values and a reader of a clean report otherwise has no way to tell this configuration from one that upgrades unconditionally. Reduce the severity where the population is known to be on-network often enough.

`Disallow` IS PRESCRIBED BY THE VENDOR DURING A STAGED ROLLOUT, temporarily and on every configuration but one, which is the one case where this finding's worst value is deliberate. Confirm whether a population is being held back on purpose before reporting it as neglect.

THE FLEET HALF OF THIS ASSERTION HAS NO COLUMN AND IS NOT DROPPED SILENTLY. That the versions actually connecting are within one major release of the one the estate treats as current cannot be read: the only operational read in the estate that could answer it returns an empty success with no counter, no row count and no timestamp, so `no agent has ever connected` and `this is never populated here` arrive identically. The current-version baseline is the customer's to supply in any case.

THE SECOND HALF OF THIS CONTROL IS BUILT NOWHERE AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIET. That access is CONDITIONED on the app version the endpoint reports - so an endpoint below the floor is refused or confined rather than asked to upgrade - rests on a HIP object's client-version criterion, which is a column of the virtual system and not of the portal. One catalogue control has one target model, and the portal took the id because this control's language leads with the portal's agent configuration, because the grading is on this half, and because this half carries the control's own severity while the other carries its lower preferred-gap tier. So a clean result here says nothing about whether an out-of-date agent would be refused. What that half would say, where it is built, is narrow in any case: the HIP matcher has exactly three children - contains, is, is-not - every one a string match with no numeric comparison anywhere beneath it, so `below the documented floor` is not something the object can express, and a HIP object no security rule references refuses nobody.
controls.rationale: Client vulnerabilities in a superseded GlobalProtect app are patched and publicly described, and the portal is the only channel that reaches the endpoints carrying them, so a portal that does not drive upgrades leaves a known-vulnerable fleet with nothing that will ever retire it.
controls.audit: Network > GlobalProtect > Portals > the portal the finding names > Agent > App Configurations. Read the upgrade behaviour on the FIRST configuration an endpoint would match, in the order the list is stored, because the portal delivers the first match and stops. On current releases the setting is delivered as a named `gp-app-config` key/value pair rather than a dedicated leaf, so confirm the key in the GUI rather than by path. A portal with no App Configurations at all is the baseline case and there is nothing to open; what to check then is whether that portal is in service. The fleet question - which app versions are actually connecting - cannot be answered from configuration and needs the customer's inventory.
controls.remediation: Set the upgrade behaviour to `Allow with Prompt` or `Allow Transparently` on the agent configurations this portal hands out, after testing the version on a limited configuration first, which is the vendor's own sequence. Where the portal hands out no agent configuration at all, the fix is to create one: nothing else reaches those endpoints. Where several values are stored on one setting, delete the entry and write it once - the list appends and the vendor's schema marks it single-valued. Pair this with a HIP-based admission condition on the app version, which is a separate piece of work on the security policy and is not asserted by this control.

queries.name: Baseline
queries.short_description: A portal whose first matching agent configuration does not tell the endpoint to upgrade, by prompt or transparently.

queries.name: Upgrades disallowed outright
queries.short_description: The agent configuration sets the upgrade behaviour to Disallow, so nothing will move an endpoint matching it and the superseded app is permanent until the portal is edited.

queries.name: Upgrades left to the user to initiate
queries.short_description: The agent configuration sets Allow Manually, so an upgrade is possible and nothing initiates it - convergence depends on individual users deciding to look.

queries.name: No agent configuration is handed out at all
queries.short_description: The portal has no client-config node, so it hands out no agent configuration and there is no upgrade instruction to read and nothing for a remediation to edit.

queries.name: No upgrade instruction recorded on the configuration
queries.short_description: An agent configuration exists and records no upgrade setting. What the agent does when the member is absent is documented as a form default and measured nowhere.

queries.name: Several upgrade values on a single-valued setting
queries.short_description: The stored list holds more than one upgrade value while the vendor's schema marks the setting single-valued, so there is no effective instruction to report.

controls.name: Agent Configuration Does Not Save User Credentials
controls.description:
A GlobalProtect portal whose agent configuration permits the app to keep the user's password on the endpoint. A laptop that is stolen, resold or compromised then carries a working remote-access credential for the corporate network in its own storage, so losing a device becomes losing network access, and revoking it means resetting that user's password rather than wiping the device.

THE LITERAL IS THE STRING `0` AND NOT THE WORD `no`. The leaf is a four-value enumeration of numeric strings - 0 is No, 1 is Yes, 2 is Save Username Only, 3 is Only with User Fingerprint - and a clause written from this control's own prose would have compared against the word and never matched anything on any device in any estate.

THE STORED ORDER IS NOT THE EXPOSURE ORDER, which is why every calibration here is an EQUALITY and none is a threshold. The column runs 0,1,2,3 and the exposure runs 0 < 2 < 3 < 1: `Save Username Only` keeps no password at all and is the mildest finding, while `Yes` keeps everything and is the worst. Any threshold over this column reports Save Username Only as worse than a stored password behind a fingerprint, and `Yes` as better than both.

`Only with User Fingerprint` IS GRADED ON WHAT IS STORED AND NOT ON WHAT GATES IT. The password is still on the endpoint; what releases it is a biometric check the firewall cannot see and that whoever holds the device may be able to satisfy. The catalogue's own notes label this value `Yes with User Fingerprint`, which points at a weaker reading than the device and the vendor agree on - both call it `Only with User Fingerprint`.

TWO SENTINELS, BOTH AT THE BASELINE. `no_agent_configuration` is a portal that hands out nothing, so what the app keeps is decided by the app; `not_set` is a configuration with no value recorded. Both are UNKNOWNS about whether a working remote-access credential is sitting in an endpoint's storage, and both the device's schema default and the vendor's documentation name `Yes` - this control's worst value - as what the form shows, so a missing reading on that question reports rather than passing.

THE HARDENED VALUE DOES NOT BY ITSELF PRODUCE A CREDENTIAL PROMPT PER CONNECTION. The authentication-override cookie is a neighbouring node on the same agent configuration and pre-empts re-entry of credentials. This control is about what is STORED on the endpoint, which is what its own node decides.
controls.rationale: A cached VPN password turns a lost laptop into a standing remote-access breach that survives the device, and clearing it means a password reset for that user rather than a remote wipe.
controls.audit: Network > GlobalProtect > Portals > the portal the finding names > Agent > App Configurations > User/User Group > Save User Credentials. Read the value on the FIRST configuration an endpoint would match, in the order the list is stored. Confirm the numeric mapping in the GUI before acting on it: 0 is No, 1 is Yes, 2 is Save Username Only, 3 is Only with User Fingerprint, and the catalogue notes label the fourth the other way round. A portal with no App Configurations is the baseline case and there is nothing to open.
controls.remediation: Set Save User Credentials to `No` on every agent configuration this portal hands out. Where the user-experience need is real, meet it with connect-before-logon and single sign-on rather than a cached password; note that the authentication-override cookie on the same configuration already suppresses re-entry of credentials, so hardening this value does not by itself add a prompt per connection. Where the portal hands out no configuration at all, what the app keeps is not under this firewall's control and the fix is to create one.

queries.name: Baseline
queries.short_description: A portal whose first matching agent configuration does not set Save User Credentials to No.

queries.name: The user's password is kept on the endpoint
queries.short_description: Save User Credentials is Yes, so both the username and the password sit in the endpoint's own storage. This is also the value the device's schema marks as the field's default.

queries.name: The password is kept behind a local biometric
queries.short_description: Save User Credentials is Only with User Fingerprint: the password is still stored and what releases it is a check on the endpoint that the firewall cannot see.

queries.name: The username is kept and the password is not
queries.short_description: Save User Credentials is Save Username Only, so no password can be lifted off the device; what remains is a confirmed account name against a confirmed portal.

queries.name: No agent configuration is handed out at all
queries.short_description: The portal has no client-config node, so what the app keeps on the endpoint is decided by the app and not by this firewall.

queries.name: No saved-credential value recorded on the configuration
queries.short_description: An agent configuration exists and records no Save User Credentials value, so whether a credential is sitting in an endpoint's storage was not established.

controls.name: Portal Web Login Page Disabled Where Nothing Needs It
controls.description:
A GlobalProtect portal that serves a browser-reachable login page. The page is an unauthenticated credential prompt published wherever the portal is reachable, it answers whether a username is real, and it is the surface PAN-OS pre-authentication exploit chains have arrived at - so an estate that distributes its agents by other means is carrying that exposure for nothing it uses.

THE ASSERTION IS THE NEGATION OF `Disable` AND THAT IS WIDER THAN AN EQUALITY ON THE SHIPPED PAGE. `custom-login-page` holds one of three kinds of value: `Disable`, which is a STATE and not a pointer and means no page is served at all; `factory-default`, the page the platform ships; or the name of an imported response page, which is any string. The third cannot be written as a placement literal and does not need to be - an imported page is still an unauthenticated credential prompt, it is graded at the same tier as the shipped one, and the negation catches it.

THE FOURTH STATE THE VENDOR HELP NAMES DOES NOT EXIST ON A DEVICE. The Help names a `None` value and calls it this field's default; the key is MANDATORY on a committed portal, measured three ways, and writing `None` is refused in both capitalisations. So the comparison is total over three states and a null is never a device state.

WHICH MEANS AN EMPTY VALUE HERE IS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE READ, and that is what this control's second query reports. A portal row whose collection did not carry `portal-config` has no login-page value, no comparison reaches a value that is not there, and SQL decides the absence the compliant way - so without a clause on the companion a portal nobody could read would appear in a clean report. `mandatory_keys_present` is that companion: it is false until something proves otherwise, and false is the firing side.

THAT COMPANION CLAUSE IS ON THIS CONTROL AND IT BELONGS TO A COVERAGE CONTROL. The rule is that a coverage statement - `we could not see this` - carries a different remediation from a configuration statement, and only the first can be cleared by the assessor rather than by the customer. No coverage control over a GlobalProtect portal exists and no build run may mint one, so the clause is parked here rather than dropped, because an unknown that reads as compliant and carries no clause at all is a silent pass. It is filed as a request and should move when that control lands.

WHETHER THE SURFACE IS NEEDED IS THE CUSTOMER'S FACT AND DELIBERATELY NOT AN APPLICABILITY CLAUSE. No column distinguishes an estate that deploys agents through endpoint management from one that relies on the page, and a clause on an unanswered question would SUPPRESS the control rather than qualify it. The standard this control holds is that serving the page is a decision somebody made and can point to, rather than the state the portal happened to be left in.
controls.rationale: An unauthenticated credential prompt on the public internet is a phishing target, a username oracle and a documented step in PAN-OS exploit chains, and an estate that distributes its agents through endpoint management gets nothing back for carrying it.
controls.audit: Network > GlobalProtect > Portals > the portal the finding names > General > Authentication > Custom Login Page. `Disable` is the only value in which no page is served; `factory-default` is the page the platform ships and any other value names an imported response page, which is the same exposure in different clothes. Where the finding says the read did not carry the portal's mandatory keys, the thing to check is the collection and not the portal - the firewall refuses to commit a portal without this key, so a blank value is not a device state. Then establish how agents are actually distributed in this estate, because that is what decides whether the page is needed at all.
controls.remediation: Set Custom Login Page to `Disable` on every portal whose agents are distributed by endpoint management or any other means. Where the page is genuinely needed, record the decision and what depends on it, and keep the portal's exposure narrowed by other means - the finding's standard is a decision somebody can point to, not the absence of the page. Replacing the shipped page with an imported one does not clear this finding: the prompt is still unauthenticated and still answers whether a username is real.

queries.name: Baseline
queries.short_description: A portal that serves a browser-reachable login page - the platform's own or an imported one - rather than disabling it.

queries.name: The platform's own login page is served
queries.short_description: The portal serves the login page the platform ships, which is the page every scanner and every published exploit chain has already seen.

queries.name: Whether this portal serves a login page could not be established
queries.short_description: The read for this portal did not carry the four keys a committed portal always has, so what it serves a browser was never established - and an unknown here reads as compliant to every comparison written over it.

controls.name: Clientless VPN Absent Unless A Business Need Is Documented
controls.description:
A virtual system that publishes internal web applications for browser access through a GlobalProtect portal, or that holds the pieces to. Publishing an application this way puts the firewall in the business of rewriting and proxying that application's pages on behalf of an internet-facing service, which is a far larger surface than a tunnel and one that has carried pre-authentication exploit chains.

THE SUBJECT IS THE VIRTUAL SYSTEM AND NOT THE PORTAL, and that is this control's central decision. What it asserts is an ABSENCE - that no portal publishes these applications AND that neither the portal nor the firewall holds the application definitions or application groups such publishing would draw on - and nothing that does not exist can carry a row. The `latent` rank is the case that forces the grain: a virtual system holding a clientless application definition that NO portal publishes has no portal row to be reported on, so a portal-keyed control is silent on it by construction. Measured in this lab on a virtual system with one definition, no portal and no interface imported.

THERE IS NO OFF SWITCH TO READ AND A READER WHO ASSUMES ONE REPORTS THE OPPOSITE. The `clientless-vpn` container has ten children on three builds measured and not one of them is a boolean - an application-to-user mapping, crypto settings, a DNS proxy, a hostname, an inactivity logout, a login lifetime, a user cap, a proxy server setting, a rewrite-exclusion list and a security zone. The UI control that looks like a top-level switch REVEALS the group rather than writing an element, so `absent OR disabled` collapses to `the element exists or it does not`, and reading the missing switch as `off` would report every portal with the feature fully configured as compliant.

NODE PRESENCE IS THE WRONG TEST AND AN ENTRY COUNT IS THE RIGHT ONE. Deleting the last entry leaves the container present and empty, deleting the container leaves `global-protect` present and empty, and an appliance in this lab carries exactly that - committed, undecorated, with a count of one answered for a container holding nothing. Every level of that residue is truthy to a naive read. BOTH OBJECT KINDS ARE COUNTED and not only the definitions, because the vendor's own sentence names two screens and an application reachable only through a GROUP would have made the estate look clean.

AN UNKNOWN FIRES AT THE BASELINE, with the engineer's questions attached. The two directions of error are different and both matter: an absence must not be reported as a decision to keep the feature off, and a presence must not be reported as an undocumented one.

ABSENCE SATISFIES THIS CONTROL RATHER THAN MAKING IT INAPPLICABLE. What is graded is PRESENCE, so there is no acceptable rank in the ordinary sense - the acceptable state is the absence of every rank below it - and a virtual system with no GlobalProtect node at all still produces a row and still reads as compliant, because this subject is a verdict over entries and not an entry.

ONE PRECONDITION IS AN APPLICABILITY CLAUSE AND THE OTHER DELIBERATELY IS NOT. The licensing clause suppresses this control ONLY where a populated licence list carries no GlobalProtect feature - a definite no. Where the appliance reported no licences at all the answer is UNKNOWN rather than no, the clause leaves the row in play and the control fires, because suppressing on an unknown reads as careful and does the opposite. The second precondition - the vendor says the feature is unsupported on a multi-vsys firewall IF the clientless traffic must traverse several virtual systems - is a statement about where traffic GOES and no configuration node holds it, so it is the engineer's question rather than a multi-vsys test that would suppress the control on every multi-vsys appliance.

THE SECOND HALF OF THIS CONTROL IS SILENT AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIET. Where a portal DOES publish, the browser sessions carrying those applications may not negotiate weaker transport than the portal itself requires - and that floor is a column of the PORTAL, not of the virtual system. One catalogue control has one target model, and there is no relation between the two models in either direction to reach the other half by. So where this control reports a live surface, the transport those sessions negotiate is unasserted by anything in this catalogue. IT IS A SECOND, INDEPENDENTLY CONFIGURED TRANSPORT ON THE SAME INTERNET-FACING SERVICE, weaker than the portal's own in every respect: four values with no TLS 1.3 at all and a schema default of TLS 1.0, against the service profile's TLS 1.0 through 1.3 and a default of 1.2. The control that looks as though it covers every TLS floor on this device does not cover this node, so read the floor on each publishing portal by hand.
controls.rationale: Clientless VPN makes the firewall rewrite and proxy an internal application's pages for anyone who can reach the portal, which is a far larger attack surface than a tunnel and has featured in pre-authentication exploit chains - and a configuration nobody uses carries all of that risk for no benefit.
controls.audit: Network > GlobalProtect > Portals > Clientless VPN, on every portal of the virtual system the finding names, and Network > GlobalProtect > Clientless Apps and Clientless App Groups for the definitions themselves. There is no checkbox to confirm this: what to look at is whether the Clientless VPN tab has applications in it and whether any application or group objects exist at all - a container that is present and empty is not the feature being in use. Where the finding says the pieces are held and nothing publishes them, the definitions are the thing to find and no portal will show them. Then establish the business need and whether each published application has been reviewed, neither of which the configuration can answer.
controls.remediation: Delete the `clientless-vpn` branch from each portal that carries it, and delete the clientless application definitions and application groups the virtual system holds - leaving the definitions behind is the `latent` state this control reports, because they are one edit from being live. Where a documented business need requires the feature, keep only the applications somebody has reviewed, record the need, and raise the clientless transport floor on each publishing portal to the highest value that node offers, which is TLS 1.2 - that floor is configured independently of the portal's own SSL/TLS service profile, defaults lower, and is asserted by no control in this catalogue. Where browser access is a real requirement, an identity-aware proxy meets it without putting the firewall in the application-rewriting business.

queries.name: Baseline
queries.short_description: A virtual system where the clientless-VPN feature is present in any degree - a portal publishing applications, or the definitions held with nothing publishing them.

queries.name: The clientless-VPN surface is live
queries.short_description: A portal carries the clientless-VPN branch and the application definitions exist, so the surface is reachable by any browser that can reach the portal.

queries.name: The pieces are held and nothing publishes them
queries.short_description: Clientless application definitions exist in this virtual system and no portal carries the branch, so nothing is reachable today and the configuration is one edit from being live.

queries.name: Whether this virtual system publishes web applications could not be resolved
queries.short_description: The clientless-VPN state of this virtual system was not established, so it is reported rather than counted as clean - an absence must not read as a decision to keep the feature off.

controls.name: Installed Content Is Recent Enough To Enforce With
controls.description:
An appliance whose applications-and-threats, antivirus or WildFire content is older than the window that content is published on, or was never installed at all, or cannot say when what it holds was published. A firewall enforces with the signatures it last received, and a frozen stream looks exactly like a working one: the configuration is correct, the schedule exists, and traffic that would have been blocked passes with nothing in the logs to say why.

IT IS THE AGE OF WHAT IS INSTALLED AND NOT THE DISTANCE FROM THE NEWEST RELEASE, and that narrowing is deliberate. Establishing that a version is current needs the publication date of the newest AVAILABLE release, which the appliance does not hold and no collection fetches. So this control reads the appliance's OWN reported release date against the windows this control's ranks name - fourteen days minimum and seven preferred for applications and threats, seven and one for the malware stream - and the half that needs the vendor's catalogue is recorded as unavailable rather than guessed.

GRADED ON ONE DERIVED COLUMN AND NOT ON TEN CLAUSES. The ranks are WINDOWS IN TIME, per stream, against two thresholds each, and a graded placement is a value-set member rather than a comparison - so the windows are computed into one ordered token at normalisation. A clause list is also one conjunction with no OR, and `any one of three streams is behind` is a disjunction no clause list expresses.

TWO OF THE SIX GRADED STATES ARE STATES THE ORIGINAL RANKS DO NOT COVER, and both are placed at this control's own severity rather than smuggled in lower. `release_date_not_reported` is an appliance that reports a content version and no publication date, so the staleness arithmetic cannot be performed at all - measured on both PA-5220s in this lab, one of which carries a real non-zero applications version. It is reported at the baseline because the stream whose currency cannot be established may BE the applications-and-threats stream, and reporting below rank 1 for a row that might be rank 1 would under-report. `stream_never_installed` is a stream with no signatures on the box at all, which is strictly worse than one merely behind.

TWO SPELLINGS OF NEVER-INSTALLED AND BOTH ARE TRUTHY. The four content streams answer `0` and the URL filtering stream answers `0000.00.00.000`, so a truthiness test passes an uninstalled stream and a numeric comparison ranks `0` as the lowest version rather than as no version. Only a comparison against those literals is right, and it is made at normalisation rather than in a clause.

WHAT A CLEAN ROW DOES NOT MEAN, and both absences are deliberate. This control's acceptable rank ALSO requires a deviation alert wired to whoever would act on it, and no column anywhere can hold that - so a pass here is the device-readable half of acceptable and silent about the alerting half. And it says nothing about whether the rest of the estate agrees with this appliance: PAN-UPD-006 owns that relative comparison and the two fail in opposite directions, so an estate uniformly a month stale satisfies that one and fails this one.

AND A LAPSED SUBSCRIPTION IS NOT AN EXEMPTION. This control's scope names an entitlement the organisation has held, which is a fact on another model and cannot be a clause here. The absence errs in the safe direction and the reason is the vendor's own behaviour: part of a content stream keeps flowing at a slower cadence after an entitlement expires, so a stream behind its window on an appliance whose licence ran out is a finding and not an inapplicable control. Whether the entitlement is live is PAN-PLT-004's subject.
controls.rationale: Content signatures are the only thing standing between a known exploit and the traffic carrying it, and they decay by the hour rather than by the release. A stream that stopped updating leaves a firewall enforcing last month's threat picture while every page of the configuration still reads as correct, so the gap is invisible to review and visible only to an attacker using something newer than the signatures on the box.
controls.audit: Device > Dynamic Updates on the appliance the finding names, and `show system info` for the same values as the device reports them. Read the VERSION and the RELEASE DATE together: a version of `0` is this platform's spelling of never-installed and is not a low version number, and a version present with no date is the state where the age cannot be computed at all rather than a state where it came out badly. The finding prints which stream and which of those two it is. Then establish the part no firewall holds: whether a deviation alert reaches whoever would act on it, which this control cannot see.
controls.remediation: Install the missing or stale content for the stream the finding names, then fix the reason it fell behind rather than only the symptom: a misfired schedule, a full disk, a lapsed entitlement or an appliance with no path to the update servers all present identically here. Where the finding says no publication date was reported, the content may be current and unverifiable - raise it with the vendor rather than reinstalling blind, because reinstalling will not add the date. Separately, wire a deviation alert to whoever would act on it; this control reports the device's state and cannot see that alert.

queries.name: Baseline
queries.short_description: An appliance whose content currency is anything other than current - behind a window, never installed, or unable to report when what it holds was published.

queries.name: Applications and threats content behind its minimum window
queries.short_description: The applications-and-threats stream is older than the fourteen-day minimum. That stream carries the vulnerability and spyware signatures and the emergency releases for vulnerabilities being exploited now.

queries.name: Malware stream behind its minimum window
queries.short_description: The antivirus stream is older than its seven-day minimum. Ranked at this control's own severity because a malware stream frozen for days is the same class of gap as a stale applications-and-threats stream.

queries.name: Content inside the minimum window and outside the preferred one
queries.short_description: Every asserted stream is inside its minimum window and at least one is outside its preferred one. What is exposed is hours of newly published signatures rather than an absent stream, which is why this is graded one tier lower.

queries.name: No publication date reported, so the age cannot be computed
queries.short_description: The appliance reports a content version and no release date, so the staleness arithmetic cannot be performed. Reported at this control's own severity because the stream whose currency is unestablished may be the applications-and-threats stream.

queries.name: A content stream was never installed
queries.short_description: A stream reports this platform's spelling of never-installed - `0`, or `0000.00.00.000` for URL filtering. There are no signatures of that kind on the appliance at all, which is worse than a stream merely behind its window.

controls.name: Subscriptions And The Support Entitlement Are Active
controls.description:
An appliance holding an expired or soon-lapsing subscription, holding no support entitlement, or unable to say what it is entitled to at all. An expired subscription degrades protection silently - threat content stops updating, URL lookups fall back to whatever the configuration says, sample submission stops - and the configuration goes on reading as correct throughout.

THE SUBJECT IS A CONCLUSION ABOUT THE LICENCE TABLE AND NOT ONE LICENCE, which is the central decision here. The commonest failing state is an entitlement that is MISSING, and a licence-keyed control has no row to report that on. A row per appliance can say `no support entitlement appears here at all`; a row per licence cannot.

TWO HALVES OVER ONE MODEL, GRADED ON TWO COLUMNS. The subscription half grades `entitlement_state` and the support half grades `support_entitlement_state`, because the two lapse independently and cost different things: a lapsed protection subscription stops a content stream, a lapsed support entitlement stops software updates - so a vulnerability in PAN-OS itself cannot be patched - and stops vendor assistance during an incident. Both halves are on this one model, so neither is silent.

ONE BASELINE AND THE SECOND HALF CARRIED BY ITS CALIBRATIONS. A control has exactly one baseline query, so the support half is expressed as the four equality queries that partition its column's failing set, each carrying that half's own assertion clause. The union is the half, because that column holds exactly one of five tokens and four of them fail. The queries are disjoint by construction and never nested, so no row takes a severity from a broader query than the one that describes it.

THE EMPTY LICENCE ELEMENT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PLACEMENT HERE AND THE DIRECTION OF THE ERROR IS WHY. `request license info` can answer with a `licenses` element that is PRESENT and EMPTY - measured on both PA-5220s in this lab - which is truthy at the envelope and empty one level in, and is not the same reply as a read that failed. The answer that shape gives is not `no licences are needed`; it is UNKNOWN. So it fires, at this control's own severity, because the entitlement that might have lapsed is unknown too. A customer told their entitlements are fine on the strength of an empty element has been told they are safe on the strength of nothing.

AN UNREADABLE EXPIRY LANDS ON THE LOWEST GRADED BAND RATHER THAN ON THE PASSING TOKEN, and that is placed rather than defaulted. The vendor's own expired flag is read first and covers the failure that matters, so what an unreadable date leaves open is only HOW SOON a live entitlement lapses - and the lowest band says that without asserting a thirty-day claim the device did not support. `Never` is a real answer and is not this case.

HOW A SUPPORT ENTITLEMENT IS RECOGNISED, AND WHICH WAY THAT ERROR RUNS. A feature name carrying the word `support` is read as one. A name matching that way which is not a support entitlement would be read as present and turn a finding into a PASS, which is the unsafe direction; it is stated here because no appliance in this lab holds a support row, so neither reading is exercised and nobody should assume it is settled.

WHAT THIS CONTROL CANNOT SAY: whether the organisation ever held an entitlement it no longer holds. The reply lists what is present, so a subscription cancelled last year and one never bought are the same absence, and only the purchase record separates them.
controls.rationale: Every subscription-delivered protection on the appliance fails quietly when its entitlement lapses, and the support entitlement is the one that decides whether the platform can be patched at all. Both are invisible on every configuration screen, so without a control reading the licence table an estate discovers a lapse when an update is refused or an incident needs the vendor.
controls.audit: `request license info` on the appliance the finding names, and Device > Licenses for the same table. Read the finding first for WHICH half failed - the subscriptions, the support entitlement, or the table being unreadable - because the three are different conversations. If the finding says the licence element came back empty, re-run the read before concluding anything: an empty element is a reply that carried no inventory, which is neither a failure nor an answer. Then check the organisation's purchase record, which is the only place a cancelled entitlement is distinguishable from one never bought.
controls.remediation: Renew the entitlement the finding names and retrieve the licence on the appliance so the table reflects it. Where no support entitlement appears at all, treat it as the first item: without one the platform cannot take a software update, so every later finding about the PAN-OS release is unfixable until it is in place. Where the finding says the licence table could not be read or came back empty, the work is to make it readable - that is an entitlement state nobody can act on, not a licence to renew. Track renewals against a horizon rather than an expiry date; this control grades thirty and ninety days ahead precisely because a renewal needs lead time.

queries.name: Baseline
queries.short_description: An appliance whose subscription entitlements are anything other than active beyond the ninety-day renewal horizon - expired, lapsing, unreadable, or an inventory that could not be read at all.

queries.name: An entitlement has already expired
queries.short_description: At least one entitlement on this appliance carries the vendor's own expired flag. The protection it delivers is on a reduced cadence or stopped, and the firewall goes on enforcing with whatever it last received.

queries.name: An entitlement lapses within thirty days
queries.short_description: At least one live entitlement lapses inside thirty days. Nothing has stopped yet, which is why this is graded below this control's own severity - what it costs is the lead time a renewal needs.

queries.name: An entitlement lapses inside the renewal horizon, or its expiry is unreadable
queries.short_description: A live entitlement lapses inside ninety days, or its expiry date could not be parsed. Both land here: the vendor's expired flag already covered the failure that matters, so an unreadable date leaves open only how soon a live entitlement lapses.

queries.name: The licence table returned no rows
queries.short_description: The licence reply carried a `licenses` element that was present and empty, so no entitlement could be checked. Reported at this control's own severity because the answer is not that no licences are needed - it is unknown.

queries.name: The licence inventory was never read
queries.short_description: No licence reply exists for this appliance, so nothing is known about what it is entitled to. An unknown fires: a pass would report subscriptions as live on the strength of a reply nobody received.

queries.name: No support entitlement appears in the licence table
queries.short_description: No feature in this appliance's licence table reads as a support entitlement. Without one there are no software updates - so PAN-OS itself cannot be patched - and no vendor assistance during an incident.

queries.name: The support entitlement has expired
queries.short_description: The support entitlement carries the vendor's own expired flag. Software updates have stopped and so has vendor assistance; the appliance goes on enforcing at the release it already holds.

queries.name: The support entitlement lapses inside the renewal horizon
queries.short_description: The support entitlement lapses inside ninety days. Nothing has stopped yet, which is why this is graded below this control's own severity.

queries.name: The support entitlement could not be established
queries.short_description: The licence table was never read, so whether a support entitlement exists is unknown rather than absent. An unknown fires at this control's own severity, because the entitlement that might be missing is the one that delivers software updates.

controls.name: A Filling Log Database Raises An Alarm Somebody Receives
controls.description:
An appliance that would not raise an alarm when a log database fills, or would raise one that reaches nobody. When a log database is full the oldest records are discarded silently, so the evidence an investigation asks for is gone and nothing on the appliance says it went.

THIS ENTRY COVERS ONE OF THIS CONTROL'S TWO HALVES AND THE OTHER IS REPORTED NOWHERE, which a reader must not mistake for a pass. The half asserted here is the log-database alarm mechanism. The half that is NOT is sustained dataplane load: there is no configuration node anywhere on the firewall holding a dataplane CPU or session-utilisation threshold, so `sustained` has no stored definition, and the vendor's own monitoring procedure instructs the reader to configure the SNMP MANAGER to watch those identifiers. The comparison is off-box by the vendor's design, so that half is discharged to an engineer's question rather than to a query - it is a measurable expression nobody can write, not a subject this control failed to reach.

GRADED ON ONE ORDERED VERDICT AND NOT ON THE NODE'S LEAVES, because the ordering is this control's and no conjunction expresses it: `on but with no threshold recorded` is WORSE than `on with thresholds and no notification route`. The master switch, the count of log types carrying a threshold and the two notification switches are resolved into one token at normalisation, and the assertion is a negated equality against the single passing one.

AN ABSENT NODE AND AN EMPTIED CONTAINER ARE DIFFERENT VERDICTS, measured. Deleting the leaves alone leaves a container that reads as PRESENT, which grades as the master switch being off rather than as an absent node - so a truthiness test on the container reports an alarm mechanism where there is none. The node being absent entirely is placed at this control's own severity, because it is the state every appliance in this lab shipped with and an appliance with no alarm node raises nothing at all.

ONE TOKEN CANNOT KEEP OFF AND UNKNOWN APART, and that is stated rather than hidden. A node present without its master switch grades the same as a node whose switch is off, because what the device does in that state is unmeasured; the column recording whether the switch was in the node at all is what a reader consults, and the direction fires either way. That column is a separate fact from the read answering - conflating the two stored `known` beside a null on two appliances, which is the circularity a companion column exists to prevent.

A SEVERITY DIRECTION THIS CONTROL DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ASSERT. A log-type threshold of `0` is storable - written, validated and committed on one lab appliance and read back as `0` from the running view - and what it MEANS is unmeasured: `alarm always` and `alarm never` are both readings and nothing on the device says which. So this control counts the log types that carry a threshold and never ranks their magnitudes. A later control that ranks the magnitude must measure that value first, because a comparison treating lower as stricter would be exactly inverted at the one value an unconfigured-looking appliance would hold.
controls.rationale: A log database that fills without warning discards the oldest records, so the first time anybody learns the appliance was over capacity is when an investigation asks for records that are no longer there. The mechanism that would have said so is one node with a master switch, a per-log-type occupancy threshold and two notification routes, and every part of it can be configured while the message still reaches nobody.
controls.audit: Device > Setup > Management > Logging and Reporting Settings on the appliance the finding names, and the node at `deviceconfig/setting/management/common-criteria-alarm-generation` for the same values. Read three things together: whether the node exists at all, whether alarm generation is on, and whether either notification route is on - the finding prints which of those failed, because the remediations differ. An EMPTY node is not an absent one, and that distinction decides which finding you are reading. Separately, this control says nothing about dataplane or session headroom; that is monitored off the appliance.
controls.remediation: Create the alarm node, switch alarm generation on, record an occupancy threshold for each log type the appliance writes, and switch on at least one notification route so a raised alarm leaves the box. ADD OR REMOVE THE WHOLE NODE RATHER THAN ITS LEAVES: an emptied container reads as present and grades differently from an absent one. Leave the parent `deviceconfig/setting/management` alone - it is shared furniture carrying settings this control does not own. Choose the threshold values from the appliance's own log volume; this control does not rank them, and what `0` means on this platform is not established. Separately, monitor dataplane and session headroom from the SNMP manager, which is where the vendor puts that comparison and where this control cannot look.

queries.name: Baseline
queries.short_description: An appliance whose log-database alarm mechanism is anything other than on, with thresholds recorded and a notification route switched on.

queries.name: The alarm node is absent entirely
queries.short_description: No master switch, no log-database threshold and no notification switch is recorded anywhere in this appliance's configuration, so nothing raises an alarm when a log database fills and the oldest records are discarded silently.

queries.name: Alarm generation is not on
queries.short_description: The node is present and alarm generation is not on, so anything configured beneath it is inert. This also covers the master switch being absent from a present node, which is the state this verdict cannot keep apart from off.

queries.name: Alarm generation is on and no log type carries a threshold
queries.short_description: There is no occupancy at which anything would fire, so the switch being on is cosmetic. Ranked at this control's own severity rather than lower: this is worse than a configured mechanism whose message cannot leave the box.

queries.name: An alarm would be raised and would reach nobody
queries.short_description: Alarm generation is on and thresholds are recorded, and neither notification route is switched on - so the alarm reaches nobody who is not already looking at the screen. Graded one tier lower because the mechanism works and the delivery fails.

controls.name: An Automatic Antivirus Content Schedule Is In Force And Applies What It Fetches
controls.description:
A firewall whose antivirus content schedule runs too rarely to keep pace with publication, or which retrieves new content and never applies it. Antivirus content publishes daily, so a cadence below a daily run leaves every signature up to six days old, and a schedule set to download without installing leaves the appliance enforcing with the content it already had while the schedule's own success reports as normal.

TWO HALVES OVER ONE CONTENT TYPE, AND EITHER ALONE PRODUCES THIS FINDING. The cadence half asks how long new content can sit unretrieved; the action half asks whether the scheduled run APPLIES what it fetches. A schedule that runs hourly and only downloads is a real failing with a faultless cadence, so the finding's sentence names which half failed - the two share this control's severity and a reader cannot tell them apart from the severity alone.

ONE BASELINE AND THE SECOND HALF CARRIED BY ITS CALIBRATIONS. A control has exactly one baseline query, so the cadence half is the baseline and the action half is expressed as the three queries that partition its column's failing set, each carrying that half's own assertion clause. The union IS the half, because the action column holds one of exactly four tokens - `download-only`, `download-and-install`, `none` and the empty string - and three of them fail.

THE ACTION HALF IS GATED ON THERE BEING A SCHEDULE AT ALL, which is stage 5's applicability clause and appears in every query carrying that half. An appliance with no antivirus schedule is reported by the cadence half ALONE: there is no run to take an action, so adding `and it does not install either` would be a second complaint about the same absence.

`none` AND THE EMPTY STRING ARE DIFFERENT ANSWERS AND BOTH FIRE. `none` is an absence that WAS read - no recurrence branch, or an explicit `none` - and is also the value the column holds for a firewall with no `update-schedule` node whatsoever, which was measured as a real committed state in this estate. The empty string is an absence NOBODY READ: the appliance's `deviceconfig/system` node came back empty and `update_schedule_collected` is false. The first is a schedule to create; the second is a collection to fix, and reporting them as the same thing would tell a customer their firewall is misconfigured on the strength of a reply nobody received.

THE PREFERRED POSTURE IS ALREADY AT THE CEILING FOR THIS CONTENT TYPE. `hourly` is the fastest cadence the grammar offers for antivirus - measured on three builds - so there is nothing better to ask for and both acceptable cadences are placed as passing rather than one being merely tolerated.

WHAT THIS CONTROL CANNOT SAY: whether the schedule has ever RUN, and whether the content it fetches was verified before it was accepted. This is a schedule and not an outcome - PAN-PLT-002 owns whether installed content is actually recent, and both controls will report on a firewall with no schedule and stale content, which stage 3 chose over a silent gap. And stage 3 records a dependency on the control that makes the firewall validate the update server's identity, because an unattended install is exactly how an unverified package would reach enforcement with nobody in the loop; that control is another domain's and no query here carries it.
controls.rationale: Antivirus content is the one protection whose value decays by the day, and a schedule is the only thing on the appliance that keeps it current without a person. A cadence below daily or a run that downloads without installing both leave the firewall enforcing stale content while every screen reports a schedule that works.
controls.audit: Device > Dynamic Updates on the appliance the finding names, or `show config running` at `deviceconfig/system/update-schedule/anti-virus/recurring`. Read the finding first for WHICH half failed - the cadence or the action - because they are different fixes. If the finding says the appliance's configuration came back empty, re-read it before concluding anything: that is a collection failure and not a schedule. And check whether the value is supplied by a Panorama template, because the merged view carries a pushed value and the store holds no row for the template's own copy.
controls.remediation: Set the antivirus schedule to run daily or hourly and set its action to download and install. Where no schedule exists at all, create one: the appliance currently retrieves nothing automatically and what it holds ages until somebody installs it by hand. Where the schedule is owned by a Panorama template, change it on the template rather than locally - a value already set locally survives a push of a different value, so a local edit can leave the two disagreeing with no sign of it on either screen.

queries.name: Baseline
queries.short_description: An antivirus schedule whose cadence is neither daily nor hourly - so `weekly`, `none`, or an appliance whose configuration was never read.

queries.name: The antivirus schedule retrieves nothing automatically
queries.short_description: No recurrence branch at all, or an explicit `none`. Nothing is checked for, downloaded or installed, and what the appliance holds ages until a person intervenes. Also the value held by a firewall with no `update-schedule` node whatsoever.

queries.name: The antivirus schedule runs only weekly
queries.short_description: The content publishes daily, so a weekly run is up to six days behind on every signature - below the floor the catalogue states, not merely short of the preferred posture.

queries.name: The antivirus schedule downloads without installing
queries.short_description: The scheduled run is `download-only`: new content is retrieved and never applied, so the appliance goes on enforcing what it already had while the schedule reports success.

queries.name: The antivirus schedule takes no action when it runs
queries.short_description: The in-force branch carries no `action` key at all, which the screen renders as `None`. Read as taking neither action - the safe direction, and the limit of what was measured.

queries.name: The antivirus schedule's action could not be read
queries.short_description: The appliance's `deviceconfig/system` node came back empty, so the action is unknown rather than wrong. An unknown fires: a pass would report the schedule as installing content on the strength of a reply nobody received.

controls.name: An Automatic Applications And Threats Content Schedule Is In Force And Applies What It Fetches
controls.description:
A firewall whose Applications-and-Threats content schedule runs too rarely, or which retrieves new content and never applies it. This is the content type that carries both application identifications and vulnerability signatures, so a cadence below a daily run can leave an EMERGENCY release unretrieved for six days, and a download-only schedule leaves the appliance enforcing the signatures it already held.

THREE VOCABULARIES FOR ONE THING, which matters when reading this finding against a screen. The screen says `Applications and Threats`, the configuration node says `threats`, and the operational command says `content`. The columns follow the configuration node because that is what a normaliser reads; the finding's own sentence follows the screen.

TWO HALVES OVER ONE CONTENT TYPE, AND EITHER ALONE PRODUCES THIS FINDING, exactly as on the antivirus control. The cadence half is the baseline; the action half is expressed as the three queries that partition its column's failing set, each carrying that half's own assertion clause, and their union IS the half because the action column holds one of exactly four tokens and three of them fail.

THE ACTION HALF IS GATED ON THERE BEING A SCHEDULE AT ALL. An appliance with no Applications-and-Threats schedule is reported by the cadence half alone: there is no run to take an action.

THIS CONTENT TYPE OFFERS A FASTER CADENCE THAN ANY OTHER AND THREE OF ITS FIVE VALUES PASS. `every-30-mins` is the fastest the grammar offers here and is the recorded preferred posture; `hourly` and `daily` both meet the floor the catalogue states. The two failing values are `weekly` and `none`, and both sit at this control's own severity.

`none` AND THE EMPTY STRING ARE DIFFERENT ANSWERS AND BOTH FIRE - an absence that was read against an absence nobody read, the first a schedule to create and the second a collection to fix.

WHAT THIS CONTROL CANNOT SAY: whether the schedule has ever run, and whether the content was verified before acceptance. Stage 3 calls this the highest-value delivery path on the device, because an unattended install here brings in application identifications and vulnerability signatures at once - which is also why it records a dependency on the control that makes the firewall validate the update server's identity. That control is another domain's and no query here carries it, so a clean row says nothing about it.
controls.rationale: Application identifications and vulnerability signatures arrive on the same schedule, and the vendor publishes emergency releases on this content type specifically. A weekly run or a download-only action means a published fix for an actively exploited vulnerability can sit unapplied for days while the firewall reports a working schedule.
controls.audit: Device > Dynamic Updates on the appliance the finding names - the `Applications and Threats` group - or `show config running` at `deviceconfig/system/update-schedule/threats/recurring`. Read the finding for WHICH half failed. An appliance whose configuration came back empty is a collection failure and not a schedule. Check whether a Panorama template supplies the value.
controls.remediation: Set the Applications-and-Threats schedule to run at least daily - every 30 minutes is the fastest this content type offers and is the preferred posture - and set its action to download and install. Where no schedule exists, create one. Where the value is owned by a template, change it on the template.

queries.short_description: An Applications-and-Threats schedule whose cadence is none of daily, hourly or every 30 minutes - so `weekly`, `none`, or an appliance whose configuration was never read.

queries.name: The Applications and Threats schedule retrieves nothing automatically
queries.short_description: No recurrence branch at all, or an explicit `none`: no automatic retrieval of application identifications or vulnerability signatures, and the value held by a firewall with no `update-schedule` node.

queries.name: The Applications and Threats schedule runs only weekly
queries.short_description: Below the floor: a weekly run can leave an emergency release unretrieved for six days, on the content type that carries vulnerability protection.

queries.name: The Applications and Threats schedule downloads without installing

queries.name: The Applications and Threats schedule takes no action when it runs

controls.name: WildFire Signatures Are Retrieved By Streaming Delivery
controls.description:
A firewall that retrieves WildFire signatures on a timed schedule rather than by streaming delivery, or not at all. What this control grades is the DELAY BETWEEN A CLOUD VERDICT EXISTING AND THE FIREWALL BEING ABLE TO ENFORCE IT: a verdict the cloud has already reached is of no use to an appliance that will not learn about it for an hour.

THE GRADING RUNS MONOTONICALLY IN DELAY AND NOT IN FREQUENCY, which reads backwards at first glance and is the one thing not to get wrong here. `real-time` is streaming and the only passing value. Every timed cadence is a finding, and the FASTER ones are graded more GENTLY: `every-min` is low, `every-15-mins` is medium, and `every-30-mins`, `every-hour` and `none` all sit at this control's own high. There is no `too often` failing on this content type, because the exposure being graded is a delay and a shorter interval is a smaller delay.

TWO PLACEMENTS SIT BELOW THIS CONTROL'S SEVERITY AND THEY ARE WHY THE CALIBRATION QUERIES EXIST. `every-15-mins` MEETS the floor the assertion names - in no case less often than every quarter of an hour - and misses the other half of the same assertion, which is the fastest cadence the deployment offers; on the public service that is `real-time`, so it is a real shortfall and the gentlest one. `every-min` is comfortably inside the floor and still short of streaming, and a minute of residual exposure is the lowest severity above informational this store can express.

ONE CLAUSE FOR THE WHOLE ASSERTION, because the acceptable set is a single member and the complement of one member is one negated equality. THE `retrieves and applies` HALF IS SUBSUMED RATHER THAN CLAUSED, and the reason is a measured trap: `real-time` and `none` carry NO `action` child at all, so the action column holds `none` on a streaming schedule - the single compliant configuration. A second conjunct asserting the action would therefore fire on EXACTLY the rows this control means to pass, and on nothing else the cadence clause had not already caught, since every timed branch is below the bar whatever its action is.

THE CADENCE CEILING DEPENDS ON WHICH WILDFIRE SERVICE FEEDS THE FIREWALL, and no column holds that. Stage 3 instructed grading against the public-service ceiling by default, so an appliance fed by a private or government cloud whose fastest option is not streaming would be reported here against a ceiling its deployment does not offer.

WHAT THIS CONTROL CANNOT SAY: whether the schedule has ever run, and whether a retrieved signature was verified before acceptance.
controls.rationale: WildFire exists to turn an unknown sample into an enforceable verdict quickly, and a timed retrieval schedule throws that away by design - the verdict waits for the next interval. Streaming delivery is the only configuration where the firewall can act on a verdict as soon as the cloud reaches it.
controls.audit: Device > Dynamic Updates on the appliance the finding names - the WildFire group - or `show config running` at `deviceconfig/system/update-schedule/wildfire/recurring`. The finding names the cadence found and the delay it implies. Confirm which WildFire service feeds this appliance before accepting the grade: this control grades against the public service's streaming ceiling, and a deployment whose fastest option is not streaming cannot reach the passing value.
controls.remediation: Set the WildFire schedule to real-time so signatures stream as the cloud reaches a verdict. Where the appliance is fed by a WildFire deployment that does not offer streaming, set the fastest cadence it does offer and record why the passing value is unreachable - the finding will persist and is then a known exception rather than an open defect. Where no schedule exists at all, create one: the appliance currently retrieves no WildFire signatures whatsoever.

queries.name: Baseline
queries.short_description: A WildFire schedule that is anything other than streaming delivery - any timed cadence, no schedule at all, or an appliance whose configuration was never read.

queries.name: WildFire signatures are not retrieved at all
queries.short_description: No recurrence branch, or an explicit `none`: a verdict the cloud has already reached never reaches this firewall. Also the value held by a firewall with no `update-schedule` node.

queries.name: WildFire signatures are retrieved hourly
queries.short_description: Up to an hour between a verdict existing and the firewall being able to act on it, against a quarter-hour floor the assertion states.

queries.name: WildFire signatures are retrieved every thirty minutes
queries.short_description: Up to half an hour between a verdict existing and the firewall being able to act on it, still beyond the floor the assertion states.

queries.name: WildFire signatures are retrieved every fifteen minutes
